resources.summary: Realistically she can claim about $1,500–$2,400 a month in combined value: SNAP and Medicaid she already has, plus WIC, child care help, Early Head Start, diapers, HEAP and Lifeline. Tomorrow: call the Help Me Grow Helpline at 1-800-755-4769 to book a WIC appointment for her pregnancy and her 2-year-old.

items.name: SNAP (Ohio Food Assistance)
items.why: She is already enrolled. Adding the new baby raises her household to 4 and should raise the monthly benefit.
items.value: About $500/mo now; more after the birth
steps: Report the pregnancy and due date to Franklin County JFS
Add the newborn within 10 days of birth
Report child care and housing costs as deductions
Complete the renewal interview on time
documents: Newborn birth certificate or hospital paper
items.verify_note: Benefit amount depends on deductions; ask the caseworker for a recalculation after the baby is born.
items.source_quote: Reporting requirements ensure AGs receive an accurate SNAP benefit amount

items.name: Publicly Funded Child Care (Ohio PFCC voucher)
items.why: Income limit is 145% of poverty. For a family of 3 that is roughly $3,200/mo; she earns $2,100 and must work or study.
items.value: Most or all of day care cost paid, often $500–$800/mo
steps: Apply through the Ohio Benefits site
Submit proof of work or school hours
Pick a provider with a Step Up To Quality rating
Report the new baby to add the infant
items.verify_note: If income later rises above 145% FPL, ask about the Child Care Choice Voucher (146%–200% FPL).
items.source_quote: Eligibility is based on 145% of the federal poverty level and at 150% for families with a child with special needs.

items.name: Early Head Start / Head Start (Child Development Council of Franklin County)
items.why: Income at or below the federal poverty guideline qualifies. Her $25,200 a year for 3 is under it. Early Head Start also serves pregnant women.
items.value: Free early learning, home visits, meals; worth $400–$700/mo
steps: Call Child Development Council of Franklin County
Ask for Early Head Start as a pregnant woman
Enroll the 2-year-old in Early Head Start
Join the waitlist if classrooms are full
documents: Proof of income (pay stubs or tax return)
items.verify_note: Confirm the nearest site to ZIP 43207 and current waitlist length by phone.
items.source_quote: Head Start services are for children from birth to compulsory school age, as well as pregnant women and expectant families.

items.name: EITC and Child Tax Credit (free help at VITA)
items.why: Working parent with two children and low income. Both credits are refundable, so she gets money even with no tax owed.
steps: Book a free VITA appointment in January
File a return even if income is low
Claim both children, including the newborn
Ask about Ohio's state credits while there
documents: Social Security cards for her and both children
Bank account number for direct deposit
Last year's tax return if she has it
items.verify_note: Newborn needs a Social Security number before filing; request it at the hospital.
items.source_quote: EITC is a refundable tax credit, which means that even if you don't owe any tax, you can still receive a refund.

items.name: WIC (Ohio Women, Infants and Children)
items.why: WIC limit is 185% of poverty; counting the unborn baby her family size is 4. SNAP and Medicaid also qualify her automatically.
items.value: Monthly food card plus fruit/veg money; free formula if needed
steps: Call 1-800-755-4769 for the nearest clinic
Book one appointment for her and the 2-year-old
Bring the child to the appointment
Ask about medical formula coverage if prescribed
documents: Proof of pregnancy or due date
items.verify_note: Being on Medicaid or SNAP makes her income-eligible automatically; say so when booking.
items.source_quote: Meets income guidelines - 185% of Federal Poverty Income Guidelines.

items.name: Food pantries and 211 (Mid-Ohio Food Collective)
items.why: Pantries in Franklin County serve by address, not by income test. Several sites serve the 43207 south side.
items.value: Free groceries weekly or twice a month
steps: Call 2-1-1 for the closest pantry to 43207
Check the pantry's open hours online
Bring bags or a cart
Ask about diapers and formula while there
items.verify_note: Each pantry sets its own visit limit; call before going.

items.name: Columbus Diaper Bank and Bloom Free Store
items.why: Columbus Diaper Bank is the National Diaper Bank Network member for her area; free stores serve children ages 0-3.
items.value: Roughly 50 free diapers a month per child, plus baby clothes
steps: Call 2-1-1 for the nearest diaper distribution partner
Register with Bloom Free Store before the first visit
Ask the WIC clinic for diaper referrals
Request newborn sizes before the due date
documents: Child's birth certificate or Medicaid card
items.verify_note: Diapers are given through partner agencies, not directly at the bank. Confirm the pickup site.

items.name: HEAP and Winter Crisis Program (Ohio energy help)
items.why: HEAP limit is 175% of poverty, about $3,930 a month for 3 people. She is well under at $2,100.
items.value: One-time bill credit, usually a few hundred dollars, plus PIPP monthly payment cap
steps: Apply online at the Ohio energy help site
Apply to PIPP Plus at the same time
Call the Winter Crisis line if shutoff is threatened
Send copies of the last 30 days of income
items.verify_note: Winter Crisis help usually opens November 1. Check the current program year dates.
items.source_quote: To qualify for HEAP, the total household income must be at or below 175 percent of the federal income guidelines for households with up to seven people

items.name: Ohio Medicaid (and Healthy Start for the children)
items.why: She is enrolled. Pregnancy coverage uses a higher income limit, and the baby is covered automatically for the first year.
items.value: $0 doctor, hospital and birth costs; also unlocks Lifeline
steps: Report the pregnancy to her county caseworker now
Pick an OB and a pediatrician in her plan
Add the newborn to her case after birth
Ask her plan about pregnancy reward programs
documents: Proof of pregnancy and due date
items.verify_note: Confirm current pregnancy and child income limits with the county office; published figures vary by source.
items.source_quote: a child is automatically eligible for medical assistance as of the child's date of birth, and remains eligible until the child reaches the age of one

items.name: Help Me Grow: home visiting and Early Intervention
items.why: Home visiting serves pregnant women and new babies. Early Intervention serves any child under 3 with a delay, with no income test.
items.value: Free nurse or coach visits, developmental checks, therapy if needed
steps: Call 1-800-755-4769 and ask for home visiting
Refer the 2-year-old if speech or walking worries her
Refer the newborn if born preterm
Keep the evaluation appointment at home
documents: Proof of pregnancy or child's birth date
items.verify_note: Preterm birth or low birth weight can qualify the baby automatically; ask the intake worker.
items.source_quote: a statewide system that provides coordinated early intervention services to parents of eligible children under the age of three with developmental delays or disabilities

items.name: Lifeline phone and internet discount
items.why: Being on SNAP or Medicaid qualifies her automatically. One discount per household.
items.value: $9.25 off a phone or internet bill each month
steps: Apply at lifelinesupport.org through the National Verifier
Upload her SNAP or Medicaid letter
Choose a participating carrier
Recertify once a year when reminded
items.verify_note: Some carriers offer free plans on top of Lifeline; compare before signing.
items.source_quote: You qualify if your household income is at or below 135% of the Federal Poverty Guidelines or if you participate in one of these programs:

items.name: Ohio Works First (TANF cash assistance)
items.why: Cash assistance uses a much lower income limit than SNAP, usually around half the poverty line. Her $2,100 is likely over it.
items.value: Small monthly cash payment if income drops; also makes Head Start automatic
steps: Ask the county worker to screen her for OWF
Reapply right away if work hours are cut
Ask about Prevention, Retention and Contingency one-time help
Ask whether a TANF letter speeds Head Start entry
items.verify_note: I could not confirm the 2026 Ohio Works First payment standard for a family of 3. Ask Franklin County JFS for the current figure.
